Program — main entry point.description: Create a complete console program. A program should define one main function and terminate with one kill statement.

Imports — standard I/O.description: Import the standard library and make the io module available. Keep the with line below ?std.

Imports — I/O and math.description: Import the standard I/O and math modules. The module list is comma-separated on the line after ?std.

Declaration — integer.description: Declare an integer variable. The initializer may be a numeric expression or another compatible value.

Declaration — floating point.description: Declare a floating-point variable. Use a decimal literal when you intend floating-point arithmetic.

Declaration — string.description: Declare a writable string buffer. The capacity in square brackets is the maximum text byte count and excludes the terminating NUL byte.

Declaration — constant integer.description: Declare an initialized integer constant. A const declaration must have an initializer and cannot be reassigned.

Declaration — fixed-width integer.description: Declare an explicitly sized integer using the type@name form.

Declaration — fixed-width floating point.description: Declare an explicitly sized floating-point value using the type@name form.

Declaration — fixed-width string.description: Declare a fixed-width string using the type@name form. Confirm the runtime representation is appropriate for the selected width.

Array — integer initializer.description: Declare a fixed-count integer array. The count inside angle brackets must match the number of initializer elements.

Array — string initializer.description: Declare a fixed-count string array. Each initializer must match the element type and the declared element count.

Array — read an element.description: Insert an array indexing expression. Array indices are zero-based; use an existing array and an in-range index.

Array — update an element.description: Assign a compatible value to an existing array element.

Function — integer result.description: Define a typed integer function. Use retreat with an expression compatible with the declared return type.

Function — floating-point result.description: Define a typed floating-point function with typed parameters and a floating-point return expression.

Function — void action.description: Define a void function for an action that does not return a value.

Function — call.description: Insert a function call with editable arguments. The compiler checks declarations and argument compatibility.

Return — return a value.description: Return a value from the current non-void function.

Return — leave a void function.description: Exit the current void function without returning a value.

Condition — if.description: Execute a block only when its condition evaluates to true.

Condition — if and else.description: Choose between two branches using if and else.

Condition — if, elif, else.description: Test multiple conditions in order. Only the first matching branch executes.

Loop — during.description: Repeat while the condition remains true. Update the condition's state inside the loop when needed to ensure termination.

Loop — repeat.description: Create a counted loop with initialization, condition, and update fields separated by commas.

Switch — cases and default.description: Branch on an integer-like value. Use arg value: for each case and at most one incase: for the default.

Record — data fields.description: Define a record with typed fields. Fields can be accessed using object.field syntax.

Record — method with self pointer.description: Define a record method. Methods use the implicit self pointer; use self~>field to access a member through it.

Alias — primitive type.description: Create a named alias for a supported primitive type.

Enum — named constants.description: Declare a set of named enum values.

Pointer — address of a variable.description: Declare a single pointer and initialize it with the address of an existing value using @.

Pointer — double pointer.description: Declare a double pointer using -->. The source pointer's address is stored in the second pointer.

Pointer — dereference.description: Read the value referenced by a single pointer using <-.

Pointer — double dereference.description: Read through two pointer levels using <--.

Pointer — member access.description: Access a record field through a pointer using the Underscore level operator ~>.

I/O — output.description: Print one value followed by a newline using the native I/O runtime.

I/O — input.description: Read one line from standard input into a string variable.

I/O — input then output.description: Read one line from the user and print a response. io.in returns a runtime-owned buffer that is reused by the next input call.

I/O — newline.description: Write a newline to standard output.

Assignment — compound addition.description: Add a value to an existing variable and store the result.

Assignment — increment.description: Increment a numeric variable by one.

Assignment — decrement.description: Decrement a numeric variable by one.

Loop control — break.description: Exit the nearest enclosing loop or switch statement.

Loop control — continue.description: Skip the remainder of the current loop iteration and continue with the next iteration.

Program exit — successful.description: Terminate the program successfully. Keep one kill statement in the main program entry point.

Comment — block.description: Insert a multi-line block comment delimited by ;- and -;.

Function — accept a string argument.description: Define a void function that accepts a string parameter and uses it. This avoids returning runtime-owned or local string storage from a function.
